rv.q: I'd recommend the production to anyone who doesn't know the play, while still feeling that it works best when presented with a minimalist austerity that matches Churchill's text.

With clever use of costume, Lyndsey Turner stretches that history to look like the last 400 years, arguing that we have been moving towards equality and that it’s time, now, to take the next step. She builds a case out of the play’s patterns.

The three men are planning the theft of a rare antique coin, the American Buffalo of the title, but Mamet is less interested in the intricacies of the heist than in revealing his characters’ dreams, insecurities and deceptions (of themselves as much as each other).
